i.norm: Verifies that calling hasNext() on a FilterListIterator advances the underlying iterator past the only matching element, so a subsequent hasPrevious() call returns false even though the underlying iterator still has a previous element. The filter's hasNext() scans forward and caches the next match. When hasPrevious() is then called, the filter undoes that scan internally, leaving the underlying iterator back at position 0 with no element before it, so hasPrevious() is false.
Build a single-element list and position the iterator at the start
Predicate that accepts only the single element
hasNext() scans forward, advancing the underlying iterator past singleElement
The underlying iterator is now past the element, so it reports a previous
The filter's hasPrevious() internally reverses the forward scan, ending up at position 0 where no previous element exists, so it returns false
